output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: In ContextAssetRequestHandler.handleAssetRequest, the `illegal` regex (^(web|meta)-inf.*|.*\.tml$, case-insensitive) is matched against ChecksumPath.resourcePath BEFORE AbstractResource.forFile() resolves the path. forFile() collapses ".." segments (see AbstractResource lines 104-131), so an attacker-supplied extraPath such as "checksum/../WEB-INF/web.xml" produces resourcePath="../WEB-INF/web.xml" which does NOT match the denylist (it starts with "../"), yet forFile() normalizes it to "WEB-INF/web.xml" and streams it — a directory traversal / protected-resource disclosure.

Fix: After calling forFile(), re-run the same `illegal` matcher against the RESOLVED resource.getPath() (which is normalized, no leading slash), and return false if it matches. Also wrap forFile() in a try/catch for IllegalStateException, which forFile() throws when the path navigates above the root (e.g. "../../etc/..."), returning false instead of surfacing a 500. Legitimate asset paths resolve to non-protected normalized paths and continue to stream as before. The original pre-resolution check is retained (it cheaply short-circuits direct WEB-INF/META-INF/.tml requests and preserves existing behavior for the null-root unit tests).

Test: Added ensure_traversal_assets_are_rejected data-driven test covering "../WEB-INF/...", "foo/../../WEB-INF/...", "../META-INF/..." and "foo/../../META-INF/..." bypass vectors, using a mocked Context so resolution stays string-only. All 8 tests in ContextAssetRequestHandlerTest pass (verified via a temporary single-class TestNG suite; suite file restored afterward).
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only adds rejection paths (returns false for traversal/protected resolutions and for above-root navigation); it does not alter handling of legitimate assets. resource.getPath() returns the normalized path without a leading slash, so the existing regex anchors (^) behave correctly. Note: the full `./gradlew --no-daemon test` task cannot reach green in this environment due to a PRE-EXISTING, unrelated defect — the untouched Groovy test ResponseCompressionAnalyzerTest declares method names containing spaces, which throws java.lang.ClassFormatError at class-load time on JDK 8 and aborts the TestNG executor regardless of suite includes. This is not caused by and not related to this patch. I therefore ran the new/affected unit test in isolation (8/8 passed) and use the compile task as the returned regression command; the project's default build command (./gradlew --no-daemon clean build -x test) also compiles the change cleanly.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-022 path traversal in Tapestry's context asset handler. ContextAssetRequestHandler screened the raw request path against a WEB-INF/META-INF/*.tml denylist, but rootContextResource.forFile() subsequently normalizes ".." segments, so a request like "fake-checksum/../WEB-INF/web.xml" (or "foo/../../WEB-INF/...") slips past the denylist yet resolves to a protected resource. The fix re-screens the resolved resource path (after "../" collapsing) and rejects any attempt to navigate above the context root, blocking access to WEB-INF/META-INF while leaving legitimate asset requests unchanged.
